role: Special Operations Forces (SOF) Team Leader / Troop Commander

evidence.quote: We planned a foot infil from an offset LZ, about forty-five minutes in, breach, clear, exploit, exfil by helicopter.
evidence.explanation: The participant organizes a multi-phase sequence of actions with timing, resources, and dependencies toward a mission objective, constituting operational planning.

evidence.quote: Really it came down to launch or delay twenty-four hours for another collection pass... There was technically a lower-signature surveillance-only option on paper.
evidence.explanation: The commander generates and weighs alternative courses of action, anticipating consequences (target movement, collateral risk) under time constraints, which is planning and course-of-action resolution.

evidence.quote: Rear wall or front gate... Between that and being able to see exactly how the rear-wall entry would go from all the rehearsals, the front gate never really competed for my attention.
evidence.explanation: The commander compares and selects among non-routine tactical options for the breach, integrating multiple information sources into a single operational decision.

evidence.quote: There was a closer casevac point off the approved list, and we could've held for a dedicated casevac asset instead of the standard bird.
evidence.explanation: The commander evaluates contingency options for extraction under compounding constraints (casualty, ISR gaps, fuel window), a non-routine problem-resolution task.

secondary_categories.subcategory: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation

evidence.quote: The SIGINT hit, which the analyst flagged as moderate confidence, not high... We also had a note from our host-nation liaison that the compound was a known family residence, kids present during the day.
evidence.explanation: The commander gathers, compares, and evaluates multiple intelligence sources of varying confidence and reliability before deciding.

evidence.quote: Team 1, my own guys, called the rear wall clean. The host-nation commandos, separately, reported ambiguous movement near that same wall.
evidence.explanation: The commander evaluates and reconciles conflicting field reports from two separate reporting elements on the same location.

evidence.quote: I'd say don't let a streak, in either direction, do your thinking for you, and don't assume today's team call is more solid than someone else's just because it's your own guys.
evidence.explanation: The participant generalizes from specific episodes to a broader principle for future decision-making, indicating abstraction and model-building from experience.

evidence.quote: The firefight sticks with you in a way that current reporting doesn't always match.
evidence.explanation: The participant reflects on how past experience forms a mental model of risk that is applied (rightly or wrongly) to new situations, an abstraction/generalization process.

evidence.quote: I was the troop commander — overall lead for the assault force, responsible for the go/no-go call, movement decisions, and the breach plan. I had a partnered host-nation commando element attached for this one too.
evidence.explanation: The participant holds overall authority for coordinating a multi-element force (organic team plus attached host-nation element) and directs mission-critical decisions.

evidence.quote: I went with Team 1's call... Between that and being able to see exactly how the rear-wall entry would go from all the rehearsals, the front gate never really competed for my attention.
evidence.explanation: The commander adjudicates between two subordinate/partnered elements' conflicting reports, a coordination and resource-allocation function over people and information.

evidence.quote: Medic called it stable but said we needed to get him out within the window.
evidence.explanation: The commander coordinates casualty evacuation logistics involving medical, aviation, and movement elements.

evidence.quote: The route crossed a wadi... There was a slower alternate route that avoided it.
evidence.explanation: The commander is directly involved in selecting and moving the force through a specific physical route and terrain feature, indicating spatial navigation as part of the task.

evidence.quote: We planned a foot infil from an offset LZ, about forty-five minutes in.
evidence.explanation: The force physically moves through terrain from an offset landing zone to the objective, evidencing navigation.

A2.3 Numeracy — no explicit numerical calculation or quantitative estimation by the participant is shown; time figures are stated but not computed on-screen.
A3.1 Serving and attending — not evidenced.

A3.3 Selling and influencing — not evidenced.

ambiguities: The closing statement to a 'junior team leader' borders on A3.2 Teaching/coaching, but since it occurs in the interview reflection rather than within the operational episode itself, it was not counted as a substantive secondary category.

evidence.quote: I was the troop commander — overall lead for the assault force, responsible for the go/no-go call, movement decisions, and the breach plan.
evidence.explanation: The participant holds direct decision authority over launch, movement, and breach method, indicating high discretion over objectives and methods within the mission.

evidence.quote: We got tasked against a facilitator, code name Zaytun... We had about six hours from tasking to launch.
evidence.explanation: The mission originates from external tasking with a fixed time window, indicating some external constraint, though the commander otherwise exercises independent judgment during execution.

evidence.quote: Team 1, my own guys, called the rear wall clean. The host-nation commandos, separately, reported ambiguous movement near that same wall.
evidence.explanation: The operation depends on coordinated reporting and action from multiple subordinate and partnered elements (Team 1, host-nation commandos, engineer, medic, liaison).

evidence.quote: Medic called it stable but said we needed to get him out within the window.
evidence.explanation: Casualty evacuation depends on cross-functional coordination between medic, aircrew, and ground element.

evidence.quote: We'd hit that valley twice before with good results.
evidence.explanation: The mission pattern (infil, breach, clear, exploit, exfil) repeats a similar operational template across multiple missions in the same area.

evidence.quote: Rear wall we'd rehearsed extensively in training — I could run that sequence in my head start to finish, exactly how the team would flow through.
evidence.explanation: The breach sequence follows a rehearsed, standardized procedure, though the overall mission requires adaptation to unique circumstances.

evidence.quote: The SIGINT hit, which the analyst flagged as moderate confidence, not high.
evidence.explanation: Key intelligence inputs are explicitly uncertain, and conditions change unpredictably (weather-degraded ISR, conflicting reports), indicating low certainty.

evidence.quote: We went in the rear wall. Found a non-combatant right near the breach point, had to pause the whole assault element to sort that out.
evidence.explanation: The commander must respond in real time to an unplanned event (a non-combatant discovery) that disrupts the mission timeline.

evidence.quote: One of my guys took a leg injury during that pause.
evidence.explanation: An unplanned casualty requires improvised adaptation of the extraction plan under time pressure.

tools.role_in_task: Signals intelligence (SIGINT) collection supporting target validation

evidence.quote: SIGINT had a phone associated with his network pinging inside the compound two nights before.
evidence.explanation: SIGINT collection is a specialized military intelligence system distinct from ordinary office ICT, used to inform the launch decision.

tools.role_in_task: Unmanned aerial system (UAS) providing ISR coverage during infiltration and extraction

evidence.quote: Primary LZ was a twenty-minute movement through ground where our ISR coverage had gaps — the UAS had been intermittent all night because of weather.
evidence.explanation: The UAS is an unmanned, digitally enabled platform performing surveillance with limited direct human control after tasking, fitting autonomous machinery/robots.

tools.role_in_task: Helicopter (casevac/exfil aircraft) operated with direct human control

evidence.quote: The casevac bird had a narrow fuel window... we landed right at the edge of the bird's fuel window, so the load was rushed.
evidence.explanation: The helicopter is a digitally enabled, directly piloted machine central to the extraction task, distinct from an autonomous system.

task_anchors.task_description: Evaluating SIGINT and a liaison civilian-presence report to decide whether to launch, delay, or surveil.
Selecting an infiltration route through contested terrain based on historical experience and current intelligence gaps.
Choosing a breach point and reconciling conflicting activity reports from two reporting elements.
Selecting an extraction LZ and casevac method under casualty and ISR-gap constraints.
